page: Microsoft Azure D2_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory and includes 51 GB of local SSD storage. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tier of modern cloud compute resources, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores consistently ranking in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is measured at 70.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 8.65 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 6.17 GB/sec for large block writes. Cryptographic and compression workloads also reflect this entry-level profile, with single-threaded gzip compression at 18.05 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 6.48 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the D2_v3 is a cost-efficient option for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads where dedicated CPU allocation is required but high throughput is not critical. It is suitable for basic web serving, small-scale Redis deployments supporting 1.11 million SET operations per second, lightweight database operations, and development or testing environments. It is not suited for intensive compute, large-scale database management, or modern machine learning tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure D2_v3 is an entry-level, general-purpose virtual machine from the Dv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core with hyper-threading. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of RAM and 51 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark evaluations place its CPU, memory, and compression performance in the lower tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 778.0 and multi-core score of 933.0. It delivers 1.32 GB/sec in static web serving and 1.11 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. This instance is best suited for low-demand workloads, such as basic web serving, lightweight database operations, and development environments requiring dedicated but modest compute resources.
